'''Jaylen Marselles Brown''' (born October 24, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played one year of [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] and was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Freshman of the Year]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. Declaring for the [[2016 NBA draft]] after his freshman season, Brown was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the third overall pick. As a professional, he has split his time between [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]].

Brown is a five-time [[NBA All-Star]], a two-time [[All-NBA Team]] member, and reached the [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference finals]] six times with Boston. He helped the Celtics reach the [[2022 NBA Finals|2022]] and [[2024 NBA Finals]], winning a championship and the [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player|Finals MVP]] award in the latter. Brown and [[Jayson Tatum]] made up the Celtics' "[[Jays (Boston Celtics)|Jays]]" duo from 2017 to 2026. He was traded by the Celtics to the Philadelphia 76ers in July 2026.

===Boston Celtics (2016–2026)===

[[File:Jaylen Brown 2017.jpg|thumb|365x365px|Brown in 2017]]
On June 23, 2016, Brown was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the third overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref name="Washburn">{{cite web |last=Washburn |first=Gary |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/celtics/2016/06/23/celtics-formed-bond-with-jaylen-brown/ukBwdoqsmOqYNvZgFKEgSL/story.html |title=Celtics formed a bond with Jaylen Brown |work=BostonGlobe.com |date=June 23, 2016 |access-date=June 27, 2016 |archive-date=September 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926054555/https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/celtics/2016/06/23/celtics-formed-bond-with-jaylen-brown/ukBwdoqsmOqYNvZgFKEgSL/story.html |url-status=live}}</ref> On July 27, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics after averaging 16.0 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.3 steals in six [[2016 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-five-players |title=Celtics Sign Five Players |work=NBA.com |date=July 27, 2016 |access-date=July 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160729204445/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-five-players |archive-date=July 29, 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Brown made his debut for the Celtics on October 26, 2016, in the season-opening 122–117 victory over the [[Brooklyn Nets]], scoring nine points on 3-for-4 shooting while also adding two blocks in 19-plus minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2016 |title=Thomas scores 25, Celtics fight off Nets 122–117 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899380 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029175358/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899380 |archive-date=October 29, 2016 |access-date=October 27, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In his first career start on November 3, Brown scored 19 points in a 128–122 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2016 |title=Cavaliers stay unbeaten with 128–122 win over Celtics |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899518 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129055718/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899518 |archive-date=November 29, 2020 |access-date=November 4, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On January 27, 2017, he scored a then career-high 20 points in a 128–98 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 27, 2017 |title=Thomas scores 21 as Celtics rout Magic 128–98 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900118 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703163418/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900118 |archive-date=July 3, 2018 |access-date=January 27, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Brown helped the Celtics claim the top seed in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] before helping them advance to the [[2017 NBA playoffs#Eastern Conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]], where the Celtics lost to the Cavaliers in five games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 26, 2017 |title=James passes Jordan, Cavs back in Finals with 135-102 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400953698 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627052729/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400953698 |archive-date=June 27, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> Brown had a productive rookie season, with his role off the bench continuing to develop as the year went on. ====2024–25 season: Coming up short====
On December 27, 2024, Brown notched a season-high 44 points, shooting 16/24 from the field with 6 three-pointers and a perfect 6/6 from the free-throw line in a 142–105 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jaylen Brown scores season-high 44 points, Celtics cruise past Pacers 142-105 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704986 |access-date=December 28, 2024 |date=December 28, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On January 30, 2025, Brown was named as a reserve for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], his fourth selection.<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama, Jaylen Brown highlight 2025 All-Star Game reserves |website=NBA.com |date=January 30, 2025 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-reserves |access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> Brown finished the regular season averaging a career-best 4.5 assists per game, reflecting improved playmaking, while maintaining a 2.6 turnover average.

In the playoffs, despite playing through a partially torn meniscus, Brown averaged 22.1 points, 7.1 rebounds, and a career-high 3.9 assists per game. Boston was eliminated in the Eastern Conference semifinals by the [[New York Knicks]], falling 4–2 in the series. In spite of losing Jayson Tatum to injury in Game 4, Brown delivered strong performances, including a near triple-double in Game 5 with 26 points, eight rebounds, and a playoff career-high 12 assists, but the Celtics were unable to extend the series and were defeated in Game 6.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Knicks beat Celtics 119-81 in Game 6 and advance to face Pacers in Eastern Conference finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401769751 |access-date=May 17, 2025 |date=May 17, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He underwent arthroscopic right knee surgery in mid-June to address the postseason meniscus tear, though Brown was expected to be fully recovered by training camp.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtics' Jaylen Brown has arthroscopic knee surgery, targets training camp return |website=NBA.com |date=June 11, 2025 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-jaylen-brown-surgery-right-knee |access-date=June 11, 2025}}</ref>

With [[Jayson Tatum]] sidelined due to an Achilles injury, Brown assumed the role of the Celtics’ primary offensive option.<ref>{{cite web |title=2025-26 Season Preview: Boston Celtics |website=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-season-preview-bos |date=October 19, 2025 |access-date=October 19, 2025}}</ref> On November 29, 2025, Brown tied his then season high by scoring 41 points and also contributed six rebounds, seven assists, and a career-high five steals in the Celtics’ 119–115 loss to the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He became the first player in the play-by-play era to record at least 27 points, five rebounds, five assists, and three steals in a first half.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edwards caps 39-point performance with unlikely 3 as Timberwolves hold off Celtics 119-115 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810148 |access-date=29 November 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On November 30, Brown recorded his fourth career triple-double with 19 points and 12 rebounds, and tied his then career-high with 11 assists in a 117–115 win over the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Payton Pritchard scores 42, Jaylen Brown gets triple-double as Celtics outlast Cavaliers 117-115 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810157 |access-date=30 November 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On December 2, Brown scored a season-high 42 points, shooting 16 of 24 to lead the Celtics to a 123–117 victory over the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |date=December 2, 2025 |title=Celtics hold off late Knicks charge to win 123-117 in rematch of East semifinal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810175 |access-date=2 December 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On December 28, Brown put up 37 points, seven rebounds, and four assists on 14-of-23 shooting from the field in a 114–108 loss to the [[2025–26 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]], extending his streak of scoring at least 30 points to nine consecutive games, tying the franchise record set by [[Larry Bird]] during the 1984–85 season.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.nba.com/news/jaylen-brown-extends-30-point-plus-scoring-streak-to-8-straight-games |title=Jaylen Brown extends 30-point-plus scoring streak to 9 straight games |website=NBA.com |date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

On January 4, 2026, Brown matched his career-high of 50 points, shooting 18-of-26 to lead the Celtics to a 146–115 victory over the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]]. He joined Jayson Tatum (5x) and Larry Bird (4x) as the only players in Celtics history to record multiple 50-point games.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 4, 2026 |title=Brown ties career high with 50 points in Celtics’ 146-115 win over Clippers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810348 |access-date=January 4, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Brown’s Complete 50-Piece, Curry’s Flurry & Philly’s MSG Takeover |url=https://www.nba.com/news/browns-complete-50-piece-currys-flurry-phillys-msg-takeover |website=NBA.com |date=January 4, 2026 |access-date=January 5, 2026}}</ref> On January 19, Brown earned his fifth [[NBA All-Star]] selection and was named a starter for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Luka Dončić, Giannis Antetokounmpo lead 2026 All-Star starters |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-all-star-starters |website=NBA.com |date=January 19, 2026 |access-date=January 19, 2026}}</ref> On January 23, Brown recorded his fifth career triple-double, posting 27 points, 10 rebounds, and a then career-high of 12 assists in a 130–126 overtime win over the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2026 |title= Payton Pritchard scores 32 and Celtics outlast Nets 130-126 in double overtime |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810492 |access-date=January 23, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On February 1, the Celtics won the NBA Pioneers Classic 107–97 over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], with Brown posting 30 points and 13 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 1, 2026 |title=Celtics win Pioneers Classic |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mil-vs-bos-0022500702 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 2, Brown won his first [[NBA Player of the Month]] award, being named the Eastern Conference Player of the Month for January. == Personal life ==
Brown is [[flexitarianism|primarily a vegetarian]] and his interests include Spanish language, history, meditation, philosophy, playing instruments, and anime.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sweeney |first=Chris |date=2018-12-04 |title=The Interview: Jaylen Brown |url=https://www.bostonmagazine.com/2018/12/04/interview-jaylen-brown-celtics/ |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=Boston Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gregory |first=Sean |date=2024-10-02 |title=How Jaylen Brown Became the NBA's Most Interesting Player |url=https://time.com/7025886/jaylen-brown-interview-time100-next-2024/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=TIME |language=en |archive-date=February 21, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250221095047/https://time.com/7025886/jaylen-brown-interview-time100-next-2024/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dabl0njGjCU |title=Finals MVP Jaylen Brown names his top 5 anime shows #NBAFinals |date=2024-06-20 |last=GQ Sports |access-date=2025-01-06 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Many have described Brown as an unusual athlete with many ambitions beyond basketball.<ref name="Letourneau">{{cite news |url=http://www.sfchronicle.com/collegesports/article/Cal-s-Jaylen-Brown-has-scholarly-ambitions-6878413.php |title=Cal's Jaylen Brown has scholarly ambitions |last=Letourneau |first=Connor |date=March 8, 2016 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |access-date=August 12, 2016 |archive-date=August 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816084440/http://www.sfchronicle.com/collegesports/article/Cal-s-Jaylen-Brown-has-scholarly-ambitions-6878413.php |url-status=live}}</ref> Brown, who is [[African Americans|African-American]], assembled a primarily African-American advisory team prior to the NBA draft, but he did not hire an agent.<ref name=Spears/> According to Marc J. Spears of [[Andscape]], one unnamed executive referred to Brown as "too smart for the league".<ref name=Spears/> 
[[File:Pemain Bola Basket NBA dari Amerika Melatih Pelajar SMA di Jakarta (42950705794).jpg|thumb|300px|Brown teaching students how to play basketball in [[Jakarta]], [[Indonesia]] in 2018 ]]
At age 22, Brown became the [[National Basketball Players Association]]'s youngest elected vice president. In recent years, he has spoken on the importance of education and technology at [[Harvard University]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], and his [[alma mater]], [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]]. In 2019, Brown was named an [[MIT Media Lab]] fellow, and he has since collaborated with the university to create ''the Bridge Program'', which mentors [[Greater Boston]] youth and high school students of color who are interested in pursuing careers in [[STEM]] programs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Person Overview ‹ Jaylen Brown |url=https://www.media.mit.edu/people/jaylen.b/overview/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117205440/https://www.media.mit.edu/people/jaylen.b/overview/ |archive-date=November 17, 2021 |access-date=November 17, 2021 |website=MIT.edu}}</ref> Through his work with MIT and his 7uice Foundation, Brown has taken a strong interest in tackling education and [[income inequality]], among other social advocacy initiatives.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rhoads |first=Julie |date=January 14, 2021 |title=Jaylen Brown is So Smart He Was Offered a NASA Internship and Became an MIT Fellow |url=https://www.sportscasting.com/jaylen-brown-is-so-smart-he-was-offered-a-nasa-internship-and-became-an-mit-fellow/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117205438/https://www.sportscasting.com/jaylen-brown-is-so-smart-he-was-offered-a-nasa-internship-and-became-an-mit-fellow/ |archive-date=November 17, 2021 |access-date=November 17, 2021 |website=Sportscasting.com}}</ref>

He was offered an [[internship]] with [[NASA]], was the youngest person to ever hold a lecture at Harvard, and was in the middle of a robotics class when he learned that his agent had secured him the largest contract in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kadlick | first=Michael | title=Jaylen Brown Gushes Over Meeting His Childhood Hero, Bill Nye the Science Guy | website=SI | date=2024-11-23 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/jaylen-brown-meeting-childhood-hero-bill-nye-science-guy | access-date=2026-02-22}}</ref>

Brown has a [[YouTube]] channel where he has posted several documentary-style video series depicting his life during the season and off-season workouts. The first episode, FCHWPO: Pawn to E4, was posted on January 31, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULT43_YP-pA |title=FCHWPO Episode 1: Pawn To E4 |date=January 31, 2017 |via=www.youtube.com |access-date=May 25, 2017 |archive-date=February 9, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209113257/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULT43_YP-pA&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live}}</ref> The video title refers to Brown's love of [[chess]]. FCHWPO, which is also his Twitter and Instagram handle, stands for "Faith, Consistency, Hard Work Pays Off."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.celticslife.com/2016/06/dont-forget-that-jaylen-brown-said-he.html |title=Don't forget that Jaylen Brown said he's ready to rip people's heads off |website=www.celticslife.com |date=June 30, 2016 |access-date=May 11, 2021 |archive-date=May 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511052132/https://www.celticslife.com/2016/06/dont-forget-that-jaylen-brown-said-he.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Brown is a practicing [[Muslims|Muslim]], having converted in 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ali |first=Hiba |date=2024-03-29 |title=10 NBA Players You Didn't Know Were Muslim |url=https://www.gqmiddleeast.com/culture/nba-players-didnt-know-were-muslim |access-date=2024-06-13 |work=GQ Middle East |language=en-US}}</ref> In June 2024, Brown performed a [[pilgrimage]] to [[Mecca]] in the form of an [[Umrah]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/nba-finals-mvp-jaylen-brown-makes-pilgrimage-to-mecca-as-he-performs-umrah-alongside-tacko-fall-after-leading-the-celtics-to-their-18th-title/ar-BB1pE7tf |title=NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown makes pilgrimage to Mecca as he performs Umrah alongside Tacko Fall after leading the Celtics to their 18th title |date=July 8, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2024 |work=[[Daily Mail]] |via=[[MSN]] |last=Callao |first=Leocciano}}</ref>

Brown is also an avid fan of [[anime]], according to Brown, his favorites are ''[[Death Note]]'', ''[[Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba]]'', ''[[Neo Yokio]]'', and ''[[The Seven Deadly Sins (manga)|Seven Deadly Sins]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Chazaro |first=Alan |date= March 5, 2025 |title=The Unbreakable Bond Between Anime and the NBA |url=https://www.gq.com/story/nba-anime |access-date=May 23, 2026 |website=[[GQ]] |publisher=[[Condé Nast]]}}</ref> Brown also watched the boxing anime, ''[[Baki (TV series)|Baki]]'' with former NBA player [[Tacko Fall]], which helped the two develop a relationship over their love for anime.<ref>{{cite web | title=NBA players who are the biggest anime fans including Daniel Gafford, Thomas Bryant, and others | website=The Times of India | date=June 24, 2025 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/anime/nba-players-who-are-the-biggest-anime-fans-including-daniel-gafford-thomas-bryant-and-others/articleshow/122044568.cms | access-date=July 12, 2026}}</ref>

In August 2026 during a farewell event in Boston, Brown was given the keys to the state of Massachusetts on behalf of the Commonwealth by Rep. Christopher Worrell for his contributions to the city of Boston during his tenure both as a player for the Celtics and his efforts to improve the community in Boston. He was also presented with a ceremonial street sign called "Jaylen Brown Way" by Boston Mayor Michelle Wu.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=Colin |date=2026-08-31 |title=Boston, Massachusetts honor Jaylen Brown with send-off gift |url=https://985thesportshub.com/2026/08/31/boston-massachusetts-honor-jaylen-brown-with-send-off-gift/ |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=98.5 The Sports Hub - Boston's Home For Sports |language=en}}</ref>
